what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 5 of 5: What fixes the binding scale?. SETTING (the owner's working reading, 2026-09-20; block 39, the open PR titled 'ail39: records that move'): a site is empty or carries ONE record; a record carries its content (six axes); two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega, omega = p, q, r for equal, opposite, orthogonal axes; a bond with an empty end weighs 1; the axioms' rule K (normalized over contents) does not depend on the scale c. MOTION: a record chooses between its position and an empty neighbouring position in proportion to the pair weights it would have there; this is in detailed balance with the static law on the occupied set. The neutral scale c_0 = 6/(p + q + 4r): an empty neighbour weighs what a record of random content weighs on average, and it is the least scale at which the law with vacancies is reflection positive through bond planes. Simulator: probes/lib/moving_gas.py p q r scale rho L sweeps seed (scale = a number or the word neutral). The overall scale c of the pair weights is invisible to the axioms' normalized rule and becomes a binding constant once records move or sites can be empty. The owner treats it as a primitive to be stated when derived or found. Block 39 gives two facts: at c_0 = 6/(p + q + 4r) an empty neighbour weighs what a record of uniformly random content weighs on average, and the law with vacancies is reflection positive through bond planes exactly for c >= c_0. TASK: examine every principled candidate and say exactly what it fixes: (a) 'no state is privileged' (the memo's sentence) applied to the empty state: does it force c = c_0, or only a relation? (b) reflection positivity with a transfer matrix that is a strict contraction on the complement of its top state: is c = c_0 (a zero eigenvalue: the empty state is then a linear combination of the record states in the transfer operator) special, e.g. does the law at c_0 coincide with the law in which an unrecorded site is integrated over contents (block 24's second reading, PR #8158)? Work this out exactly on windows where block 24's two readings differ. (c) the formation rate z Z_x: is there a scale at which it is independent of the neighbourhood for every neighbourhood, or only on average? (d) consistency between formation and motion: a record formed at x and moved to y against a record formed at y. (e) anything that would tie c to the memo's open gate on the natural unit. Deliver exact finite computations for each candidate and the statement of what it determines. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/moving-what-fixes-the-scale/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route.
